schema: Six non-null I64 columns: id, customer, symbol, day, qty, price
consistency: Read-your-writes in one process; DuckDB native batches flush before acknowledgement
durability: In-memory only. No process/power-loss durability or replication claim.
atomicity: No cross-call transaction. Valid batches and adapter argument rejection are tested; general engine error/OOM atomicity remains unqualified.
idempotency: None: IDs are unique by construction, not enforced by a primary-key constraint
retry: No mutation retries; any unexpected error fails the case
query_path: Parsed SQL INSERT VALUES versus quoted-target Rayfall insert, including source parsing
typed_path: DuckDB C Appender + per-batch flush versus Rayforce C typed vectors/table + fixed Rayfall dispatch
append_payload: id=x, customer=x%10000, symbol=x%256, day=x%30, qty=1+x%100, price=100+x%9901
read_and_cache_scope: Fresh in-memory processes load the same CSV; reads are hot/recent, not OS-cold
oracle: Every old and new row is exported in ID order and matched to independently generated canonical CSV bytes by length and SHA256
timing: Actual first-write-start to last-write-finish includes intervening dispatch/logging and the middle read for multi-request cells. Setup, initial/final read and export are separately timed.
limits: Single writer; no distributed or availability claim. Both engines use the same CPU/memory cap. Native adapter batches contain 1..10000 rows. CSV witness exports are verification artifacts, not engine persistence.
